questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (4.2,0);\coordinate (A) at (2.1,3.94953);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$4.2\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\pic[draw,"$62^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.95cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=R--L--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The end of an A-frame tent is $4.2$ m wide and each sloping side makes $62^{\circ}$ with the ground. Find the height of the tent at its centre, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Used the full width of $4.2$ m instead of halving it to get the base of the right-angled triangle.
Divided by $\tan62^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying, treating the height as the denominator.
Used $\cos62^{\circ}$, which gives the sloping side rather than the height.

questions.solution_text:
The height splits the tent into two right-angled triangles, each with a base of $2.1$ m.
$\tan62^{\circ}=\frac{h}{2.1}$
$h=2.1\tan62^{\circ}$
$=3.9495\ldots$
$\approx3.95\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.5]\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (9.0,0);\coordinate (D) at (4.5,0);\coordinate (A) at (4.5,3.4);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$9.0\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\draw[dashed] (A)--(D) node[midway,right] {$3.4\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(D)!0.5cm!(R)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(D)!0.5cm!(A)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(D)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=1.5cm,angle eccentricity=1.35] {angle=R--L--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A gable end is $9.0$ m wide and its ridge is $3.4$ m above the wall top. Find $\theta$, the angle each rafter makes with the horizontal, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Used the full width of $9.0$ m as the base instead of halving it.
Swapped the height and the half-width, using $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4.5}{3.4}\right)$.
Used $\sin^{-1}$, treating the $4.5$ m half-width as the length of the rafter.

questions.solution_text:
Half of the gable is a right-angled triangle with a base of $4.5$ m and a height of $3.4$ m.
$\tan\theta=\frac{3.4}{4.5}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.4}{4.5}\right)$
$=37.0730\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx37^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.45]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (D) at (3.39148,0);\coordinate (B) at (9.63511,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.39148,5.42751);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,above left] {$6.4\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(B);\draw (C)--(D);\coordinate (va) at ($(D)!0.55cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(D)!0.55cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(D)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=B--A--C};\pic[draw,"$41^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.35] {angle=C--B--A};\node[below left] at (A) {$A$};\node[below right] at (B) {$B$};\node[above] at (C) {$C$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A bridge truss has a vertical post $CD$ from the apex to the deck. Given $AC=6.4$ m, find the length of the chord $BC$, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Stopped at $DB$, the length along the deck, instead of the sloping chord $BC$.
Gave the height of the post $CD$ rather than going on to the second triangle.
Used $\cos58^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin58^{\circ}$ when finding the post.

questions.solution_text:
First find the post $CD$, the side the two triangles share.
$\sin58^{\circ}=\frac{CD}{6.4}$
$CD=6.4\sin58^{\circ}$
$=5.4275\ldots\text{ m}$
Now use $CD$ in the right-hand triangle.
$\sin41^{\circ}=\frac{5.4275\ldots}{BC}$
$BC=\frac{5.4275\ldots}{\sin41^{\circ}}$
$=8.2729\ldots$
$\approx8.27\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.42]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (D) at (3.33436,0);\coordinate (B) at (10.83436,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.33436,3.45283);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,above left] {$4.8\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(B);\draw (C)--(D);\draw (D)--(B) node[midway,below] {$7.5\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(D)!0.6cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(D)!0.6cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(D)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$46^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.6cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=B--A--C};\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=0.75cm,angle eccentricity=1.35] {angle=C--B--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A gable end has an off-centre ridge on a vertical post. The left rafter is $4.8$ m long and rises at $46^{\circ}$, and the foot of the post is $7.5$ m from the right-hand wall. Find $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

options.why: Swapped the post and the $7.5$ m run, using $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{7.5}{3.45}\right)$.
Used the $4.8$ m rafter itself as the height of the post instead of finding the post first.
Used $\cos46^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin46^{\circ}$ when finding the post.

questions.solution_text:
First find the post, the side the two triangles share.
$\sin46^{\circ}=\frac{h}{4.8}$
$h=4.8\sin46^{\circ}$
$=3.4528\ldots\text{ m}$
Now use $h$ in the right-hand triangle.
$\tan\theta=\frac{3.4528\ldots}{7.5}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3.4528\ldots}{7.5}\right)$
$=24.7203\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx25^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (D) at (3.71573,0);\coordinate (B) at (6.14973,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.71573,2.8);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (A)--(C);\draw (C)--(B);\draw (C)--(D) node[midway,right] {$2.8\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(D)!0.3cm!(B)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(D)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(D)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$37^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.95cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=B--A--C};\pic[draw,"$49^{\circ}$",angle radius=1.1cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=C--B--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A truss has a vertical post $2.8$ m high, with chords meeting the deck at $37^{\circ}$ and $49^{\circ}$. Find the total span of the truss along the deck, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Multiplied by each tangent instead of dividing, so both parts of the deck came out wrong.
Found only the left-hand part of the deck and forgot to add the right-hand part.
Used sine instead of tangent, which gives the two sloping chords rather than the deck.

questions.solution_text:
The post divides the span into two right-angled triangles.
$\tan37^{\circ}=\frac{2.8}{p}$
$p=\frac{2.8}{\tan37^{\circ}}$
$=3.7157\ldots\text{ m}$
$\tan49^{\circ}=\frac{2.8}{q}$
$q=\frac{2.8}{\tan49^{\circ}}$
$=2.4340\ldots\text{ m}$
Span $=3.7157\ldots+2.4340\ldots$
$=6.1497\ldots$
$\approx6.1\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: A triangular sail is right-angled at the tack. Its vertical leading edge is $6.0$ m and the angle between that edge and the sloping leech, measured at the head, is $31^{\circ}$. Find the total length of edging needed for all three edges, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Added only the vertical edge and the foot, leaving the sloping leech out of the total.
Divided by $\tan31^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying when finding the foot.
Used $\sin31^{\circ}$ instead of $\cos31^{\circ}$ when finding the leech.

questions.solution_text:
With the right angle at the tack, the $31^{\circ}$ angle at the head has the foot opposite it and the $6.0$ m edge adjacent to it.
$\tan31^{\circ}=\frac{a}{6.0}$
$a=6.0\tan31^{\circ}$
$=3.6052\ldots\text{ m}$
$\cos31^{\circ}=\frac{6.0}{c}$
$c=\frac{6.0}{\cos31^{\circ}}$
$=6.9997\ldots\text{ m}$
Edging $=6.0+3.6052\ldots+6.9997\ldots$
$=16.6050\ldots$
$\approx16.6\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (P) at (0,0);\coordinate (Q) at (3.19094,0);\coordinate (S) at (0.84547,1.35304);\coordinate (U) at (2.34547,1.35304);\draw (-0.7,0)--(P);\draw (Q)--(3.89,0);\draw[dashed] (P)--(Q);\draw[very thick] (P)--(S) node[midway,above left] {$x\text{ m}$};\draw[very thick] (Q)--(U) node[midway,above right] {$x\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (S)--(U) node[midway,above] {$12\text{ m}$};\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=Q--P--S};\pic[draw,"$58^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.65cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=U--Q--P};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A lifting bridge has two identical sections, each $x$ m long, hinged at opposite banks. Lowered, they exactly span the river. Raised to $58^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, their tips are $12$ m apart. Find the width of the river, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found $x$, the length of one section, and stopped instead of doubling it for the river.
Divided the $12$ m gap by $\cos58^{\circ}$ rather than by $1-\cos58^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
Lowered, the sections span the river, so the river is $2x$ m wide.
Raised, each section covers a horizontal distance of $x\cos58^{\circ}$, and what is left over is the gap.
$2x-2x\cos58^{\circ}=12$
$2x(1-\cos58^{\circ})=12$
$2x=\frac{12}{1-\cos58^{\circ}}$
$=25.5275\ldots$
$\approx25.5\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (L) at (0,0);\coordinate (R) at (3.2,0);\coordinate (D) at (1.6,0);\coordinate (A) at (1.6,2.88648);\coordinate (S) at (0.66517,1.2);\coordinate (U) at (2.53483,1.2);\draw (L)--(R) node[midway,below] {$3.2\text{ m}$};\draw (L)--(A);\draw (A)--(R);\draw[very thick] (S)--(U);\draw[dashed] (D)--(1.6,1.2) node[midway,right] {$1.2\text{ m}$};\pic[draw,"$61^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=R--L--A};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The end of an A-frame tent is $3.2$ m wide and its sloping sides make $61^{\circ}$ with the ground. A horizontal spreader bar is fixed across the tent $1.2$ m above the ground. Find the length of the spreader bar, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Subtracted the offset at one end of the bar only, forgetting the matching offset at the other end.
Gave the two offsets added together instead of what is left of the $3.2$ m width.

questions.solution_text:
At each end of the bar the ground, the sloping side and the $1.2$ m height form a small right-angled triangle.
$\tan61^{\circ}=\frac{1.2}{d}$
$d=\frac{1.2}{\tan61^{\circ}}$
$=0.6651\ldots\text{ m}$
Bar $=3.2-2\times0.6651\ldots$
$=1.8696\ldots$
$\approx1.87\text{ m}$
